h1: The 8 Best Monitor Arms Under $100 for Desks and Walls, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Monitor Arm Under $100: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 8 monitor arms under $100 compared on weight limits, reach, clamp range, cable routing and wall or desk mounting.
summary: The Pholiten gas-spring arm is the best monitor arm under $100, holding screens up to 35 inches and 24 pounds. The Pivotix is the best desk arm with cable routing, the ErGear dual stand is the best for two screens, and the ErGear wall mount has the longest reach.
intro: A monitor arm should vanish: the screen floats where you want it and stays there. The mistake that breaks that is weight. Many buyers pick an arm for its price or look and only discover at assembly that the limit is 17 pounds and their monitor weighs 20. So we ranked each arm by weight limit first, then reach, clamp range and cable handling.

We reviewed eight arms from their listings, four desk-mounted and four wall-mounted, all well under $100 by their price bands. Many cost less than $30, which leaves budget for a second arm. Test and range figures are manufacturer claims.

products.name: Pholiten Adjustable Single Monitor Mount, Gas Spring, 17-35 Inch
products.verdict: A gas-spring desk arm for monitors up to 35 inches and 24 pounds.
products.description:
The Pholiten is a single desk arm with a gas spring that moves the screen up and down with a light push. It fits monitors from 17 to 35 inches and up to 24 pounds on 75 by 75 or 100 by 100 VESA patterns, and it switches between landscape and portrait orientation.

It ranks first because it carries the highest weight limit among the single desk arms and the widest size range, which means it fits the majority of monitors, including some ultrawides under 24 pounds. Against the Pivotix it offers a gas spring, which holds position more smoothly than a mechanical spring, but gives up the built-in cable management the Pivotix lists.

Buy it for a standard desk and a monitor in the 24 to 34 inch range. It sits in the under $30 price band, far under the budget. The caveat is that the listing gives no reach figure or clamp thickness, so measure your desk edge.
products.idealFor: Most single-monitor desks with a 24 to 34 inch screen.
products.skipIf: You need a wall mount or two screens.

products.name: Pivotix Long Reach Monitor Arm, Spring-Assisted, 17-32 Inch
products.verdict: A spring-assisted desk arm with built-in cable routing and a quick-release plate.
products.description:
Pivotix uses a mechanical spring to assist height changes, with tilt, swivel and 360 degree rotation, and fits flat or curved screens from 17 to 32 inches up to 19.8 pounds. It has built-in cable routing, a C-clamp for desks 0.6 to 2.2 inches thick and a detachable VESA plate for quicker mounting.

It sits second because it lists a clamp range and cable management, which the Pholiten leaves out, but its weight limit is lower. The long reach lets you pull the screen toward you. It beats the monTEK wall arm for desks where wall drilling is a problem.

Buy it if you want a tidy desk and an easy install. It sits in the under $30 price band. The caveat is the 19.8 pound limit, which rules out heavy ultrawides.
products.idealFor: Desk owners who want clean cables and a quick setup.

products.name: ErGear Dual Monitor Stand, Heavy Duty Desk Mount, Up to 32 Inch
products.verdict: A side-by-side dual arm with 31 inches of span and full tilt and swivel.
products.description:
The ErGear dual stand holds two monitors up to 32 inches each, with a 31.22 inch arm span, a 16 inch pole, plus or minus 90 degree swivel, plus or minus 45 degree tilt and 360 degree rotation. It offers two installation options, clamp or grommet, with labeled hardware.

It ranks third because two screens need a stronger stand, and this one costs less than two single arms. It beats the stacked MOUNT PRO for desks that want side-by-side screens. The listing sets conditions for each monitor, so read size and weight limits before ordering.

Buy it if you run two screens next to each other. Its price band is $30 to $50. The caveat is that the pole stays on the desk, which uses surface area.

products.name: ErGear Monitor Wall Mount, Full Motion Single Arm, 13-34 Inch
products.verdict: A full-motion wall arm that retracts to 3.54 inches and extends to 20.47.
products.description:
This ErGear wall arm fits 13 to 34 inch monitors up to 19.8 pounds on 75 or 100 mm VESA patterns. It retracts to 3.54 inches, extends to 20.47 inches, gives 12.2 inches of height adjustment, and tilts plus 80 and minus 50 degrees with plus or minus 90 swivel.

It ranks fourth because wall mounting clears the desk entirely, and its extension range is the largest of the wall arms here. It beats the monTEK on reach, but you must find studs or concrete. It sits behind the desk arms because installation takes drilling.

Buy it if desk space is tight and the wall has a stud behind it. Its price band is under $30.
products.idealFor: Small desks and shared walls with a stud.

products.name: MOUNT PRO Stacked Vertical Dual Monitor Stand, up to 32 Inch
products.verdict: A vertical dual arm with a 31 inch pole for one screen above the other.
products.description:
The MOUNT PRO stacked stand puts one monitor above another on a 31 inch center pole, and holds up to 17.6 pounds per arm. It fits 13 to 32 inch screens, supports both C-clamp and grommet installation, and lets each screen tilt and swivel.

It ranks fifth because stacking suits a narrow set of workflows, such as coding or trading, and because 17.6 pounds per arm is a lower limit than the Pholiten's. It beats the side-by-side dual for narrow desks.

Buy it if desk width is the limit. Its price band is $30 to $50. The caveat is that the top monitor needs a neck tilt, so keep it for reference material.
products.skipIf: You prefer screens side by side.

products.name: monTEK Single Monitor Wall Mount, Full Motion Spring Arm, 17-32 Inch
products.verdict: A spring-loaded wall arm with 90 degree tilt and a quick-release plate.
products.description:
The monTEK is a full-motion wall arm for 17 to 32 inch screens up to 19.8 pounds on VESA 75 or 100. It tilts plus or minus 90 degrees, swivels 180 degrees, rotates 360 and retracts when idle, with a quick-release VESA plate. It is made of steel and aluminum.

It ranks sixth because it offers a bigger tilt range than the ErGear wall arm, but its listing is less specific on reach. The listing warns against mounting to drywall alone, which is the right advice for any arm.

Buy it if you want spring-assisted motion on a wall. Its price band is $30 to $50.
products.idealFor: Wall-mounters who want smooth spring motion.

products.name: VIVO Single Ultrawide Wall Mount, Up to 49 Inch, 44 lb
products.verdict: A steel wall arm that holds ultrawide screens up to 49 inches and 44 pounds.
products.description:
VIVO's wall arm supports ultrawide monitors up to 49 inches and 44 pounds on VESA 75 and 100 patterns. It collapses flat against the wall and extends 10.5 inches, with plus 5 to minus 12 degrees of tilt, plus or minus 45 degrees of swivel and plus or minus 3 degrees of leveling. It has built-in cable management.

It ranks seventh because its motion range is limited. It is the only arm here that carries a heavy ultrawide, and at the under $30 price band that is unusual.

Buy it for a big ultrawide on a stud wall. Skip it if you want much motion.
products.idealFor: Ultrawide owners with a stud wall.
products.skipIf: You want a lot of adjustment.

products.name: MOUNT PRO Single Monitor Wall Mount, 13-32 Inch, Height Adjustable
products.verdict: A full-motion wall arm listed with a 20000 cycle test claim.
products.description:
The MOUNT PRO wall mount fits 13 to 32 inch screens on VESA 75 and 100, with plus 90 to minus 45 degree tilt, 180 swivel and 360 rotation. The listing claims a 20000 cycle test, and says it fits wood stud and concrete walls.

It ranks last because the listing gives no weight limit, and the reach is not specific. It is solid but less detailed than the ErGear wall arm.

Buy it if you want a plain wall arm. Its price band is $30 to $50.
products.idealFor: Basic wall mounting for a standard monitor.
products.skipIf: You need published weight and reach numbers.

methodology.description: Published weight ratings and screen size ranges were compared, since a monitor that is too heavy will droop.

methodology.description: Every arm costs less than $50, so the budget has plenty of room for a second arm or a better monitor.

whatMatters.detail: Every arm has a limit, from 17.6 pounds per arm up to 44 pounds. A monitor over the limit sags or tilts forward. Weigh your screen, which the spec sheet states, and leave 10 percent spare.
The four screw holes on the monitor back are spaced 75 by 75 mm or 100 by 100 mm on most screens. Every arm here supports both. If your monitor has no holes, you need an adapter plate.
A clamp grips the desk edge, and it only works within a range, for example 0.6 to 2.2 inches on the Pivotix. Glass desks and edges with a lip need a check. Grommet mounts need a hole.

Gas springs move smoothly and hold position, and mechanical springs are cheaper and work for lighter loads. Wall arms may be spring-assisted or fixed. If you change height often, choose gas or spring.
A wall arm must go into a stud, brick or concrete, never drywall alone. Use a stud finder, and check how far the arm extends. Renters should skip wall mounts or confirm the lease.

cards.text: A clamp that fits your desk thickness, cable routing, and a weight limit above your monitor.

cards.text: Pholiten for most, Pivotix for clean cables, and the dual ErGear for two screens.

cards.text: You want gas-spring arms for heavy monitors or want to mount three screens. Those start above $100.

cards.text: You have one standard monitor. The Pholiten does it for under $30.

faq.a: If it has a 75 by 75 or 100 by 100 mm VESA pattern and weighs under the arm's limit, yes. Check the monitor spec sheet.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake?
faq.a: Ignoring weight. A 20 pound monitor on a 17 pound arm droops, so match the limit to your screen.

faq.q: Is the Pholiten worth it over the Pivotix?
faq.a: If you want a gas spring and a higher weight limit, yes. If you want cable routing and a listed clamp range, the Pivotix is the better fit.

faq.q: How do I install a desk clamp?
faq.a: Place the clamp at the desk edge, tighten until firm and test the arm before mounting the monitor. Add a protective pad on soft desks.
Not on its own. Use studs, brick or concrete, and follow the arm's instructions for lag bolts.

faq.q: Do dual arms need strong desks?
faq.a: Yes. A dual pole puts torque on the desk edge, so use a solid desk of at least 0.6 inch thickness.

finalTake: The Pholiten is the best monitor arm under $100 for most desks, thanks to its gas spring and 24 pound limit. The Pivotix adds cable routing, the ErGear Dual covers two screens, and the ErGear wall arm clears the desk. Weigh your monitor before you buy, and leave a margin under the arm's rating.
